get.summary: Resolve Record Type by Source Type
get.description: Given a source document's type key (e.g. a Document Management document type id), returns the active record type imported or linked to that source so it can be auto-applied, or an empty body when no active match exists (the caller then lets the user pick a manual applicable type).

parameters.name: source_type_key
parameters.description: Source-system type key (e.g. a Document Management document type id) to resolve.

parameters.name: Accept-Language
parameters.description: Locale for localized response messages (for example: en, fr-FR, pseudo)

source.description: Where the record type originated: ASSETS (manually defined) or DOCUMENT_MANAGEMENT (imported).

applies_to.description: Attachment origins this record type applies to.

items.description: Attachment origins this record type applies to.

source_type_stale.description: For source-added (e.g. DOCUMENT_MANAGEMENT) record types, true when the linked source type is no longer active in the source tool, so the admin should delete this row. Null when not applicable (ASSETS-sourced) or when the source could not be checked.

display_order.description: Admin-configured position of this record type within its company list.

400.description: The server could not understand the request due to invalid syntax or parameters that fail to meet validation requirements.

401.description: Although the HTTP standard specifies "unauthorized", semantically this response means "unauthenticated". That is, the client must authenticate itself to get the requested response.

403.description: The client does not have access rights to the content; that is, it is authenticated, but the server is refusing to give the requested resource. Unlike 401, the client's identity is known to the server.

404.description: The server can not find the requested resource. This can mean either the URL is not recognized, or the resource itself does not exist. Servers may also send this response instead of 403 to hide the existence of a resource from an unauthorized client.

import http.client

conn = http.client.HTTPConnection("localhost:8080")

headers = {
    'Procore-Company-Id': "SOME_INTEGER_VALUE",
    'Accept-Language': "SOME_STRING_VALUE"
    }

conn.request("GET", "/rest/v2.0/companies/1234/projects/1234/assets/record_types/resolve?source_type_key=SOME_STRING_VALUE", headers=headers)

res = conn.getresponse()
data = res.read()

print(data.decode("utf-8"))
